features.user_story_today: A user's or package's spec:// links resolve exactly. Embeds, the compiler, agent prompts and documentation citations go through one resolver that checks containment and gives typed refusals. Installed slots are checked against the lock content hash (slot_integrity=verify), and the slot record lists each file as converted or copied, with its sha256. There is no CLI or MCP command that prints the text of one section given its spec://…#anchor address. MCP read_doc covers documentation pages, and `vibe explain --fragment` shows code, not spec text. When a package's Markdown fails Markdown-to-XML conversion during install, the file is copied silently.
features.worth_doing: Two small behaviours. (1) During install, warn when an opposite-format spec document fails conversion and is copied instead, and optionally add a strict mode that refuses (M-01-C.4). (2) Possibly add a thin read-section-by-address surface (`vibe show section <spec://…#a>` plus an MCP tool) on top of the existing resolver (M-01-D.1/D.2). This is an owner decision. Everything else (world-authority objects, proof strengths, digest carriers, parity reports) has no user value.

features.user_story_today: Declared sources work today: package [sources]/source_exports descriptors and host project.sources policy, ordinary Markdown outlines, and raw XML-data and opaque resources that are kept and not converted. Migration of legacy sources is done. `vibe tree` (JSON, plain and TUI) shows each package's effective boot load, its STATIC contributions with byte and line counts, and nested embed spans. `vibe why` explains the admitting chain. `vibe prompt check` reports lane size against a context window. After `vibe install` or `vibe update`, a closure diff shows lock changes and the byte change of the boot lanes. `vibe init` keeps the host XML/Markdown dialect and leaves generated lanes out of package content. There is no pre-install what-if preview of how boot would change, no two-snapshot compare in the TUI, and long Windows paths for slot materialisation have not been tested on Windows.
features.worth_doing: Mostly nothing. Optional and owner-gated: let `vibe install --plan-only` show the boot-lane change before applying (the D/E cluster, cut down to one flag). Separately, a native Windows check of long slot paths with an actionable diagnostic if it fails (G.4, tied to BACKLOG B-132). A full debugger service, a richer inspector and derivative parity overlap the IDE stage and M-10.

features.user_story_today: Nothing a vibe CLI user can notice. Nothing outside those modules calls read_saved_change, ChangeIdentityAnalysis or plan_change_migration. No CLI or MCP command exists, and this repository has no change.toml. Without that decision, nothing: the library foundation is done, and the rest is fixtures or IDE overlay work.

Override layers (`[layers]` targets with policy overridable and replace/supplement relations; crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/layers.rs, crates/vibe-cli/tests/cli_layer_relations.rs) replace or extend a dependency's spec unit locally and are visible in tree, capture and compose. `vibe registry vendor` mirrors packages locally. features.user_story_today: A user runs `vibe create` or `vibe verify` (CLI) or the MCP `lifecycle_run` tool with phase create/verify. Another node's parked task is refused, and a busy workspace is refused through the lease.

features.user_story_today: A consumer can configure a dependency in vibe.toml under [requires.configurations]: features, groups with cardinalities and fallbacks, named profiles, typed parameters (bool, integer, text, choice, path), optional dependencies, strong and weak forwarding, and declared subskills. `vibe install` evaluates the configuration for each candidate inside the resolvo solve. vibe.lock keeps the original consumer input apart from the resolved features, dependencies and causes. Changing only the intent makes the lock stale. `vibe reinstall` replays the exact choices, and `vibe update` refuses changed defaults until the user reviews them. Choices can be previewed or answered with `vibe show configuration-preview` (also through MCP), an answer file (`--configuration-input`) or interactive PTY prompts. Unsupported setups refuse before any write: the naive/sat/embedded solver cells, `exclude` masks on a configured owner, conditional/OR requirements on a configured owner, and uninstalling a configured package. Today no package in this repository's vibepacks declares [configuration] or [features].
features.worth_doing: Two concrete gaps. (1) `vibe uninstall` refuses any package that has a configuration record or that a configured package selected. (2) The legacy `--features` / `--all-features` / `--no-default-features` flags are ignored on a bare `vibe install` when the lock is fresh, and `vibe reinstall` does not replay them. Everything else is either already delivered or a widening of explicit refusals that no current package needs (other solver cells, masks, conditional owners, migrating legacy [features], Redbook variants).

features.user_story_today: A maintainer builds each native bundle from one pinned commit (`cargo xtask dist build`, which checks every binary's `--version`), creates or replaces a draft GitHub release for that version, uploads bundles, then `dist finalize` downloads and digest-checks all five targets against commit/tree before publishing. The `.github/workflows/release-distributions.yml` workflow_dispatch drives this, with optional --checks/--tests/--self-check. End users' install.sh/ps1/cmd scripts check the bootstrap's sha256 against the published manifest. An installed-bundle smoke (`init` + `install flow:wal` + `tree`) runs only for x86_64-apple-darwin.
features.worth_doing: Run the same installed-bootstrap smoke for all five targets in the release workflow. That would stop a release whose bootstrap is broken on Linux or Windows from reaching users. It is a CI change, so the owner must approve it. The rest (formal plan subjects, A/B approval policy, producer signatures, recovery journals, equivalence proofs) gives users nothing.

features.user_story_today: Today a user can install, update, roll back and uninstall applications into their own HOME with `vibe install -g` and `vibe app ...` (crates/vibe-app). Uninstall refuses when other installs depend on the app, `vibe app rollback` restores the previous version, interrupted runs resume, `vibe storage gc` removes unused payloads, and `vibe app exec` plus version files pick which version runs. Downloads are checked against their digests, mirrors can serve them, and archives are unpacked with links and file modes kept. There is no code for Docker, BuildKit, OCI, rootfs, pacman/Arch, service discovery or egress control (a grep of crates/*/src for docker|buildkit|rootfs|pacman|oci finds only a purl type string). None of the 30 M-15 tasks has an accepted prototype, and all of them are 'planned-only / outside-old113'.

The one small concrete gap is that `vibe bin` picks the debug binary whenever one exists, even when it is stale. Building container or rootfs environments from vibe packages is a real future product direction, but whether to build it at all is an open owner decision (BACKLOG B-233, environment-target-design-disposition.md). If the owner says yes, the first useful step is the 'same app, host plan vs synthetic rootfs plan, refuse when no executor' journey on top of vibe-app's planning, not the 30-task A–K ladder.

features.user_story_today: A program can drive vibe today in two ways. It can run CLI commands with the global `--json` flag, plus `--progress-format json` / `VIBE_PROGRESS_FORMAT` for a machine progress stream. Or it can start `vibe mcp` and call 16 MCP tools over stdio JSON-RPC (migration plan/operation, configuration preview, subskill read/materialise, explain/query/select, lifecycle_tasks/lifecycle_run, requirements_query, read_doc). Unattended commands refuse instead of prompting (e.g. scrape requires --assume-yes). Deploy has its own intent journal and recovery, and parked lifecycle runs resume. There is no negotiated session, no cross-domain submission journal, no unsaved-buffer analysis and no MCP progress or cancel.
features.worth_doing: One small concrete fix: the MCP tools query, select and explain do not enforce the input schema they advertise. A wrong-typed `limit` silently becomes 50, `json:"true"` silently becomes false, and unknown fields are ignored. They should refuse with InvalidArguments, as lifecycle_run and requirements_query already do. Everything else (census, universal registry, framed session, submission dedup, editor overlays/barriers) has no current client and should be dropped, or deferred to the IDE stage if that stage actually needs it.

features.user_story_today: A user or program can get the project/package tree as JSON with `vibe tree --json` (the model is in crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/tree/model.rs, checked by tests/tree_json.rs). They can query traceability with explain/query/select from the CLI and MCP, and query requirements through one shared owner from both. There is no package rename or move command, no multi-client editing protocol, no MCP tree tool and no mechanically checked operation coverage matrix.

Moving the tree model out of the CLI into a shared crate is worth doing only when the IDE tree/search stage consumes it. The conformance and coverage gates (C.*, D.1) are re-proving or bookkeeping and should be dropped.
